account:
Today has appeared mostly routine, and I have not established that anything secret or unusual is happening. I have a lingering feeling that town affairs may be passing me by, but that is a suspicion, not evidence. My market visit produced no evidence of a bread shortage or trouble. At the afternoon accounts review, the builder reported no confirmed defects from visual checks of the bridge, landing, and warehouse approach. Freight said the warehouse was empty and there were no confirmed orders, and offered to quote for authorized deliveries and keep the ferry available. Those appear to be ordinary efforts to find work, not evidence of a hidden undertaking. The innkeeper attended, but I repeatedly could not make out their words, so their business remains unknown to me.

The accounts are incomplete: the secretary said they had not seen an accounts ledger and could not verify the balance or commitments. I personally checked the treasury and found 128 emeralds. No spending was authorized. This is an administrative gap worth following up, but I do not know whether it reflects anything beyond missing records.

At tea, my neighbour reported a quiet afternoon and no unusual activity or fresh riverside news since returning home. The secretary has helped record findings and reminded me of appointments. On returning to the office, I saw the secretary place a written book into the appointments chest twice. I do not yet know the books' identities or contents, and have asked about them, along with afternoon visitors and correspondence. Filing books there could be entirely routine. My next priority is to hear the secretary's answer and examine the relevant records rather than assume a conspiracy.
